subject: Agriculture
title: Food Sovereignty
description: A fast breakdown of Food Sovereignty for builders.

hook.text: Food sovereignty says communities—not corporations or trade rules—should control their own food systems.

buildup.text: La Via Campesina—a global peasant movement of 200 million members—coined the term in 1996.

discovery.text: Food sovereignty includes the right to grow traditional crops, save seeds, and sell locally without corporate interference.

twist.text: Trade agreements often override local food policies. WTO rules can force countries to accept food imports they don't want.

climax.text: Food sovereignty is law in Ecuador, Bolivia, Mali, and Nepal. It challenges the global free-trade food model.

punchline.text: Who decides what a nation eats? The farmer or the market? That's the question.

quiz.question: What does food sovereignty demand?
options: Community control over food systems instead of corporate or trade-rule dominance
